title: Nine hundred and fifty years
hookLine: Nuh calls his people by night and by day, openly and in private, and few listen (71:5–9; 29:14)
last: HABIL — ONE LIFE IS LIKE ALL LIVES.

cards: A teacher stands in front of a room where nobody's listening. Phones out, heads down, someone asleep in the back. She says it again, another way.
Tries a joke. Tries a story. Stays after class in case anyone wants to ask.
Almost nobody does. Now stretch that across many lifetimes. Nuh, Noah, is remembered for a boat.
But the Qur'an spends whole passages on something else: how long he kept talking to people who wouldn't listen.

teach.h: MY LORD, I'VE CALLED THEM NIGHT AND DAY.
teach.b: A whole surah carries his name, surah seventy-one, and most of it is his own report to God. Paraphrasing: my Lord, I've called my people night and day, and my calling has only made them run further away.

Every time I called them, so You could forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and pulled their clothes over their heads. I called them openly. I spoke to them in public, and I spoke to them in private.
Night and day, loud and quiet, crowds and one at a time: he tried everything. And what was he asking? Not much: ask your Lord's forgiveness; He is forgiving.
He promised them rain, and gardens, and rivers. Then the number.
In Pickthall's words, “he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years.” Some scholars take it as it stands.
Others note it describes how long he stayed among his people, and differ over how it fits his whole life. Either way, it's patience almost too long to imagine. And the result?
The Qur'an is honest: only a few believed with him.

By the world's measure, that looks like failure. But a hadith in Bukhari, about the Day of Judgment, has people coming to Nuh and calling him the first messenger to the people of the earth, and a grateful servant.
His success wasn't counted in listeners. It was counted in the calling.

how: Muslims honor Nuh as a prophet, and surah seventy-one, which bears his name, is read as a lesson in patient, persistent calling.

o: give up; they've made their choice.
call again: night and day, openly and in private.
games.why: he tried every way there was, for nine hundred and fifty years. the calling itself was the faithfulness.

practice: Sit quietly and say, slowly, the words Nuh asked of his people: I ask God's forgiveness. Give each word its own breath, and repeat it a few times without hurrying. If you don't pray, let the words be a simple wish to begin again.

wordCard.voice: Nuh. Noah: the prophet who called his people night and day for nine hundred and fifty years, while only a few listened.

orig.note: Arabic: "a thousand years less fifty," the Qur'an's way of saying nine hundred and fifty (29:14).

carryVoice: Your line: call anyway. Few listened, and he never stopped calling. See you tomorrow.
